regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 76, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.31
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A green/social/sustainability label has to be earned, not just claimed. The money must fund projects that fit a recognised standard (like ICMA, Climate Bonds, ASEAN, EU or an Indian framework), and for sustainability-linked bonds the targets must fit such a standard. On top of that, an independent outside reviewer — paid in a way that avoids conflicts and genuinely expert in ESG — must check the bond, through a second opinion, verification, certification or scoring. That independent check is what guards against 'greenwashing' (claiming to be green without really being so).
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The label is earned by external verification against a named standard, not self-declared — the independence and expertise conditions on the reviewer are what protect against greenwashing. A registered credit rating or ESG rating provider can act as reviewer, subject to the same independence conditions.
regulation_content.practical_point: Pick the recognised standard first, then appoint an independent, conflict-free, ESG-expert reviewer and choose the review type that suits investors. A reviewer whose pay or ties compromise independence is exactly the greenwashing risk inspectors look at.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: issuer. Evidence standard alignment, reviewer independence and expertise, and the review output.
regulation_content.risk_point: A reviewer with a fee structure or relationship that compromises independence is the greenwashing-adjacent risk an inspection probes.
regulation_content.interview_point: What distinguishes a 'green' bond from a 'sustainability-linked' bond under Reg 76, and what independent-review safeguards apply to each?
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of ESG-labelled debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.chapter_title: ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE (ESG) LABELLED DEBT SECURITIES
regulation_content.provision_heading: Additional disclosures in Offer document / Information Memorandum
regulation_content.regulation_text:
77. Additional disclosures in Offer document / Information Memorandum

 (1) The issuer shall make the following additional disclosures in the offer
 document or information memorandum, as the case may be, in respect of
 ESG labelled debt securities (other than sustainability-linked debt
 securities):

 (a) A statement on ESG objectives of the issue of debt securities;

 (b) Details of process followed by the issuer for evaluating and
 selecting the project(s) and/or asset(s);

 (c) Proposed use of the proceeds of the issue including details of the
 project(s) and/or asset(s); and

 (d) Details of the systems and procedures to be employed for tracking
 the deployment of the proceeds of the issue.

 (2) The issuer shall make the following additional disclosures in the offer
 document or information memorandum, as the case may be, in respect of
 sustainability-linked debt securities:

 (a) The issuer shall disclose the rationale for issuance of
 sustainability-linked debt securities and consistency with issuers’
 overall sustainability and business strategy.

 (b) The issuer shall adhere to pre-issuance and post-issuance
 obligations in accordance with the relevant international standards
 that the securities are aligned with.

 For example, where the debt securities are aligned with ICMA
 Sustainability-Linked Bond Principles (2024), the guidelines
 related to five core components - Selection of Key Performance
 Indicators, Calibration of Sustainability Performance Targets,
 Bond characteristics, Reporting and Verification shall be followed
 for all the disclosures and continuous obligations.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 77, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.32
regulation_content.simple_explanation: ESG bonds need extra disclosures, which differ by type. 'Use-of-proceeds' bonds (green, social, sustainability) must explain their ESG goals, how projects are chosen, how the money is used, and how spending is tracked. 'Sustainability-linked' bonds must explain why the targets fit the company's strategy and how they follow the recognised standard's before-and-after obligations (for example, the ICMA principles). One discloses where the money goes; the other discloses the targets and what happens if they are missed.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The disclosure split tracks the instrument logic: use-of-proceeds bonds disclose where the money goes; sustainability-linked bonds disclose the KPIs, targets and structural consequences of missing them.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of ESG-labelled debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.chapter_title: ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE (ESG) LABELLED DEBT SECURITIES
regulation_content.regulation_text:
78. Additional Continuous Disclosure Requirements

 (1) The issuer shall provide the following additional disclosures to the
 recognised stock exchange(s), at least on an annual basis, until full
 utilisation of the proceeds, in respect of ESG labelled debt securities (other
 than sustainability-linked debt securities):

 (a) Utilisation of proceeds of the issue;

 (b) Allocation: List of project(s) and/or asset(s) to which proceeds of
 the debt securities have been allocated/invested, including a brief
 description of such project(s) and/or asset(s), and the amounts
 disbursed:

 Explanation: Where confidentiality agreements restrict the
 disclosure of details about specific project(s) and/or asset(s), the
 information shall be presented in generic terms or on an
 aggregated portfolio basis; and

 (c) Impact:

 (i) Qualitative performance indicators and, where feasible,
 quantitative performance measures of the expected/achieved
 ESG impact of the project(s) and/or asset(s).

 (ii) Where the quantitative benefits/impact cannot be ascertained,
 then the said fact may be appropriately disclosed along with
 the reasons for non-ascertainment of the benefits/impact on
 the ESG.

 (iii) The methods and the key underlying assumptions used in
 preparation of the performance indicators and metrics shall
 be disclosed.

 (2) The issuer of sustainability-linked debt securities shall provide the
 following additional disclosures to the recognised stock exchange(s), at
 least on an annual basis, and additionally for any date or period relevant for
 assessing the performance of Sustainability Performance Targets (SPT)
 which may lead to a potential adjustment of the debt securities’ financial or
 structural characteristics:

 (a) up-to-date information on the performance of the selected Key
 Performance Indicator(s), including baselines where relevant;

 (b) any information enabling investors to monitor the level of
 ambition of the SPTs; and

 (c) a verification report by an independent external reviewer outlining
 the performance against the SPTs and the related impact, and
 timing of such impact, on the debt securities’ financial and/or
 structural characteristics.

 CHAPTER XI: LISTING OF OTHER FINANCIAL PRODUCTS
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 78, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.33
regulation_content.simple_explanation: After issue, ESG bonds must keep reporting — at least once a year until all the money is used. Use-of-proceeds bonds report how much was spent, on what, and the impact (they can group figures where confidentiality needs it). Sustainability-linked bonds report how they are doing against their targets, plus an independent reviewer's report checking that performance and whether it changed the bond's terms (like the interest rate). That independent verification report is the item most often forgotten until it is due.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The post-issuance regime is where ESG labels are kept honest — annual allocation and impact reporting for use-of-proceeds bonds, and verified SPT tracking for sustainability-linked bonds. The verification report is the item most likely to be overlooked until it is due.
regulation_content.practical_point: Set a yearly ESG reporting reminder tied to how the money is used, and line up the reviewer early for the target-verification report on sustainability-linked bonds. Late or missing reports undermine the label.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: issuer. Provide annual allocation/impact (use-of-proceeds) or KPI/SPT and verification disclosures (sustainability-linked) until full utilisation.
regulation_content.risk_point: Missing or late annual impact/SPT verification disclosure undermines the label and is a visible continuous-disclosure breach.
regulation_content.compliance_frequency: At least annually until full utilisation of proceeds
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of ESG-labelled debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.provision_heading: Listing of Funds and Investment Trusts
regulation_content.regulation_text:
79. Listing of Funds and Investment Trusts

 An issuer may list a fund or an investment trust on a recognised stock exchange
 in terms of IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 79, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.34
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A fund or investment trust can be listed under the separate IFSCA Fund Management Regulations, 2022. This rule is just the cross-link into that fund regime — the listing sits on the fund's approval there, so the two sets of rules are read together.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is the cross-reference into the FME framework — the listing sits on the fund's authorisation under the FM Regulations, so read the two regimes together.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of funds, investment trusts, commercial paper, certificates of deposit and other permitted products

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
80. Listing of Commercial Papers

 An issuer may list commercial paper on a recognised stock exchange in such
 manner and subject to such conditions as may be specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 80, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.34
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Commercial paper (a short-term corporate IOU) can be listed on the terms the regulator specifies. This is an enabling pointer; the detailed terms must first go through public consultation and regulator approval (see Reg 130).
regulation_content.regmate_comment: An enabling pointer — Reg 130(2) requires the norms under Regs 80, 81, 82 (and 126) to be settled through public consultation and Authority approval.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of funds, investment trusts, commercial paper, certificates of deposit and other permitted products

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
81. Listing of Certificates of Deposit

 An issuer may list certificate of deposit on a recognised stock exchange in such
 manner and subject to such conditions as may be specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 81, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.34
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Certificates of deposit (a bank's short-term deposit instrument) can be listed on the terms the regulator specifies — with the detailed terms, like those for commercial paper, subject to public consultation first.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of funds, investment trusts, commercial paper, certificates of deposit and other permitted products

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
82. Listing of other financial products

 An issuer may list such other financial product on a recognised stock exchange
 in such manner and subject to such conditions as may be specified by the
 Authority.

 CHAPTER XII: LISTING OBLIGATIONS AND DISCLOSURE
 REQUIREMENTS
PART A: GENERAL OBLIGATIONS
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 82, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.34
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Other financial products can also be listed on the terms the regulator specifies, again subject to public consultation before the terms take effect. This keeps the framework open to new products without leaving the conditions undefined.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of funds, investment trusts, commercial paper, certificates of deposit and other permitted products

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
83. Applicability

 The provisions of PART A of this Chapter shall apply to the securities listed on
 the recognised stock exchange(s) under these regulations.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 83, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.35
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Part A of Chapter XII sets the common set of ongoing duties (the 'listing obligations') that every listed security must follow, before the product-specific parts add anything extra on top.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Part A is the common LODR baseline — every listed security inherits it before the security-specific parts (B to E) layer on.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities under these regulations

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
84. Principles governing disclosures and obligations

 The Listed Entity shall make disclosures and abide by its obligations under these
 regulations in accordance with the following principles:

 a) Information shall be prepared and disclosed in accordance with applicable
 accounting standards for financial disclosure;

 b) The Listed Entity shall implement the applicable accounting standards in
 letter and spirit in the preparation of financial statements taking into
 consideration the interest of all stakeholders, and shall also ensure that the
 annual audit is conducted by an independent and qualified auditor;

 c) The Listed Entity shall refrain from misrepresentation and ensure that the
 information provided to recognised stock exchange(s) and investors is not
 misleading;

 d) The Listed Entity shall provide adequate and timely information to
 recognised stock exchange(s) and investors;

 e) The Listed Entity shall ensure that disseminations made under the
 provisions of these regulations and circulars issued thereunder, are
 adequate, accurate, explicit, timely and presented in a simple language;

 f) The Listed Entity shall ensure that the channels for disseminating
 information provides for equal, timely and cost efficient access to relevant
 information by investors;

 g) The directors of the Listed Entity shall act in good faith in order to promote
 the objects of the company for the benefit of its members as a whole, and
 in the best interests of the Listed Entity, its employees, the shareholders,
 the society and for the protection of environment.

 h) The Listed Entity shall abide by all applicable laws of its home jurisdiction
 as well as securities laws and also such other requirements as may be
 specified by the Authority and the recognised stock exchange(s).

 i) The Listed Entity shall make the specified disclosures and follow its
 obligations in letter and spirit taking into consideration the interest of all
 stakeholders.

 j) The Listed Entity shall ensure that the relevant filings, reports, statements,
 documents and information are duly filed within the specified timelines and
 contain requisite information.

 k) The Listed Entity shall ensure that periodic filings, reports, statements,
 documents shall contain information that shall enable investors to track the
 performance of a Listed Entity over a period of time and shall provide
 sufficient information to enable investors to assess the current status of a
 Listed Entity. It shall include all material updates on the business, financial
 performance, management, etc.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 84, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.35
regulation_content.simple_explanation: These are the guiding principles behind all the ongoing duties — follow proper accounting, get an independent audit, do not mislead, give complete and timely information, give everyone equal and low-cost access to it, let directors act in good faith, follow the law, and file periodic information on time. When a specific rule is unclear, the regulator reads it in light of these principles.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: These principles are the interpretive lens for every specific LODR obligation — where a rule is silent or a judgment call arises, the Authority reads it back to these principles.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities under these regulations

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
85. General obligation of compliance

 The Listed Entity shall ensure that key managerial personnel, directors,
 promoters, controlling shareholders or any other person dealing with it comply
 with responsibilities or obligations as assigned to them under these regulations.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 85, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.35
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The listed company must make sure that its key managers, directors, promoters, controlling shareholders and others who deal with it actually follow their own duties under these rules. So compliance is not only about the company's own filings — it also means making sure its people meet their individual obligations.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This casts an oversight duty on the entity for the conduct of its control persons — compliance is not only the entity's own filings but ensuring its people meet their individual obligations.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities under these regulations

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
86. Compliance Officer and Obligations

 (1) A Listed Entity shall appoint a qualified company secretary as the
 compliance officer:

 Provided that where the entity is incorporated outside India, a company
 secretary or equivalent shall be appointed as compliance officer.

 (2) The compliance officer of the Listed Entity shall be responsible for-

 (a) ensuring conformity with the applicable regulatory obligations under
 these regulations, in letter and spirit;

 (b) co-ordination with and reporting to the Authority, recognised stock
 exchange(s) and depositories with respect to compliance with rules,
 regulations and other directives of these authorities in such manner as
 may be specified; and

 (c) ensuring that the correct procedures are followed to ensure the
 correctness, authenticity and comprehensiveness of the information,
 statements and reports filed under these regulations.

PART B: ENTITIES WITH SPECIFIED SECURITIES LISTED ON
RECOGNISED STOCK EXCHANGES AS A PRIMARY LISTING
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 86, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.36
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Every listed company must appoint a qualified company secretary (or the equivalent, if it is a foreign company) as its Compliance Officer. This person makes sure the company follows the rules, deals with and reports to the regulator, exchange and depositories, and keeps the systems that ensure filed information is accurate and complete. This role is the hub of the whole compliance system — almost every ongoing disclosure runs through the Compliance Officer.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The compliance officer is the statutory nerve centre of the LODR regime — nearly every event-based and periodic disclosure in Part B runs through this role. For foreign-incorporated entities, the 'or equivalent' recognises jurisdictions without the CS designation, but the accountability is identical.
regulation_content.practical_point: Appoint the Compliance Officer at listing, write their reporting lines to the regulator, exchange and depositories into the compliance manual, and build the disclosure calendar around them. Leaving this role empty or powerless is treated as a serious system failure.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Board / Compliance Officer. Evidence the appointment, qualification and defined responsibilities of the compliance officer.
regulation_content.risk_point: A vacant or under-empowered compliance-officer role is a systemic control failure that an inspection treats as going to the heart of LODR compliance.
regulation_content.interview_point: What are the three statutory responsibilities of the compliance officer under Reg 86, and who may hold the role for a foreign-incorporated Listed Entity?
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
87. Material or Price Sensitive Information

 (1) The Listed Entity shall immediately make disclosure to the recognised
 stock exchange(s) of any event or information concerning it or any of its
 subsidiaries or associates which, in the opinion of the board of directors of
 the Listed Entity, is material or price sensitive.

 Explanation 1: The Listed Entity shall consider the following criteria for
 determination of materiality of events/ information:

 (a) the omission of an event or information, which is likely to result
 in discontinuity or alteration of event or information already
 available publicly;

 (b) the omission of an event or information which is likely to result in
 significant market reaction if the said omission came to light at a
 later date; or

 (c) where the criteria specified in sub-clauses (a) and (b) are not
 applicable, an event/information may be treated as being material
 if in the opinion of the board of directors of Listed Entity, the event
 / information is considered material.

 Explanation 2: For the purpose of these regulations, immediately shall
 mean promptly but not later than twenty four hours.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall frame a policy for determination of materiality,
 based on criteria specified in these regulations, duly approved by its board
 of directors, which shall be disclosed on its website.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 87, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.36
regulation_content.simple_explanation: If something important or price-sensitive happens (about the company or its group), the company must tell the exchange immediately — and 'immediately' means as soon as possible and no later than 24 hours. What counts as 'important' is a judgement call, so the company must have a board-approved policy (published on its website) explaining how it decides. The 24-hour clock is the number people remember, but the real skill is judging materiality well and writing down the reasoning.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The twenty-four-hour outer limit is the number that matters, but the harder discipline is the materiality judgment itself — the criteria (omission causing discontinuity, likely market reaction, or board opinion) are deliberately principle-based, so the board's documented reasoning is the defence. A published materiality policy is both a mandate and the framework against which the Authority tests specific calls.
regulation_content.practical_point: Approve and publish a materiality policy, and set up a fast process that can assess an event and disclose within 24 hours. For every borderline event, write down why you did or did not disclose — a documented reason is your defence.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Trigger: any potentially material/price-sensitive event. Deadline: disclosure within 24 hours. Record the materiality assessment and disclosure.
regulation_content.example: On a Friday evening, a subsidiary loses a big customer contract. The company must assess it and, if important, disclose it within 24 hours — the weekend does not pause the clock.
regulation_content.risk_point: Late disclosures and 'we didn't think it was material' calls are the most common problems here. No written assessment turns a defensible judgement into a finding.
regulation_content.interview_point: An unclear event happens at 6 pm. How do the 24-hour rule and the materiality test drive your disclosure decision?
regulation_content.important_numbers: Materiality disclosure 'immediately' = promptly, not later than 24 hours
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.provision_heading: Amendment to Memorandum or Articles of Association
regulation_content.regulation_text:
88. Amendment to Memorandum or Articles of Association

 The Listed Entity shall immediately disclose to the recognised stock exchange
 (s) any amendment to its constitutional documents viz. memorandum or articles
 of association or any other similar document, by whatever name called.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 88, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.37
regulation_content.simple_explanation: If the company changes its constitution (its memorandum or articles — the documents that set its rules and shareholder rights), it must tell the exchange immediately, because such changes can affect the rights attached to the listed securities.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Constitutional changes can alter rights attaching to listed securities, so the exchange must learn of them without delay.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Disclose constitutional amendments immediately.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
89. Intimation about Board Meeting

 (1) The Listed Entity shall give prior intimation about the meeting of the board
 of directors and immediately disclose outcome of the meeting of the board
 of directors, to the recognised stock exchange(s) in respect of any of the
 following proposals:

 (a) dividends;

 (b) buyback of securities;

 (c) decision with respect to fund raising or change in capital;

 (d) financial results;

 (e) decision on voluntary delisting by the Listed Entity from stock
 exchange(s);

 (f) any material business event such as acquisition, demerger, sale or
 purchase of assets/ businesses/ companies; and

 (g) material litigation.

 (2) The intimation required under sub-regulation (1) shall be given at least two
 working days in advance, excluding the date of the intimation and date of
 the meeting.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 89, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.37
regulation_content.simple_explanation: For certain board meetings, the company must warn the exchange in advance and disclose the outcome immediately. This covers meetings about dividends, buybacks, raising money or changing capital, financial results, voluntary delisting, big business moves (like an acquisition, demerger or asset sale) and major court cases. The advance warning must be given at least 2 working days before the meeting — and you count neither the day you give notice nor the day of the meeting. That counting trap catches people out.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The two-working-day advance intimation is a market-fairness device — it warns the market that a price-sensitive decision is imminent. The exclusion of both the intimation and meeting dates from the count is the computational trap.
regulation_content.practical_point: Build the board calendar so notices go out at least 2 clear working days ahead (excluding both the notice day and meeting day), and pre-draft the outcome announcement so it can go out right after the meeting.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Trigger: board meeting on a listed matter. Prior intimation ≥2 working days; outcome disclosed immediately.
regulation_content.example: A board meeting to consider a dividend is set for Wednesday. Because you exclude both the notice day and the meeting day, the latest you can send prior intimation is the previous Friday (2 clear working days before).
regulation_content.risk_point: Mis-counting the two clear days, or omitting a triggering agenda item from the intimation, are the routine slips inspection catches.
regulation_content.interview_point: A board meeting to consider dividend is set for Wednesday. Applying Reg 89's exclusion rule, what is the last permissible date to issue prior intimation?
regulation_content.important_numbers: Prior intimation of board meeting ≥2 working days (excluding intimation and meeting dates)
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
90. Annual and Extraordinary General Meetings

 The Listed Entity shall immediately disclose to the recognised stock
 exchange(s) the proceedings of Annual and extraordinary general meetings, by
 whatever name called.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 90, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.37
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must tell the exchange immediately what happened at its shareholder meetings (annual or extraordinary). These meetings can pass resolutions that move the share price or shift control, so the market needs to know quickly.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: General-meeting proceedings can carry resolutions that move price or control, so prompt disclosure keeps the market level.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Disclose AGM/EGM proceedings immediately.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.provision_heading: Change in Director, KMP, Auditor or Compliance Officer
regulation_content.regulation_text:
91. Change in Director, KMP, Auditor or Compliance Officer

 (1) The Listed Entity shall immediately disclose to the recognised stock
 exchange(s) any change in director, key managerial personnel, auditor or
 Compliance Officer.

 (2) In case of a resignation of the auditor of the Listed Entity, detailed reasons
 for resignation of auditor, as given by the said auditor, shall be disclosed
 by the Listed Entity to the recognised stock exchange(s) as soon as possible
 but not later than one working day of receipt of such reasons from the
 auditor.

 (3) In the case of a resignation of any director, key managerial personnel or

 compliance officer, such person shall inform to the recognised stock
 exchange(s), in writing if he is aware of any irregularities which would have
 a material impact on the Listed Entity, including financial reporting, as soon
 as possible but not later than one working day.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 91, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.37
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Any change in a director, key manager, auditor or Compliance Officer must be disclosed immediately. Two situations have a tighter 1-working-day deadline: if an auditor resigns, the detailed reasons must be disclosed within 1 working day; and a director, manager or Compliance Officer who is leaving and knows of a serious irregularity must inform the exchange in writing within 1 working day. An auditor walking away is often the first outside sign of trouble, so those reasons cannot be buried.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The one-working-day auditor-resignation-reasons rule targets the governance red flag — an auditor walking away is often the earliest external signal of trouble, so the reasons cannot be buried. The parallel duty on a departing officer to flag known irregularities is a whistle-adjacent safeguard.
regulation_content.practical_point: Keep a ready process to capture an auditor's resignation reasons and a departing officer's declaration, and disclose within 1 working day. Sitting on auditor-resignation reasons is a very visible governance breach.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Trigger: change/resignation of director, KMP, auditor or CO. Immediate disclosure; auditor reasons / officer irregularities within 1 working day.
regulation_content.risk_point: Suppressing or delaying auditor resignation reasons is a high-visibility governance breach.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Auditor resignation reasons / director-KMP-CO irregularity intimation within 1 working day
regulation_content.compliance_frequency: Event-based (immediate; auditor/CO reasons within 1 working day)
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
92. Adverse opinion by auditor

 The Listed Entity shall immediately disclose to the recognised stock
 exchange(s) any adverse opinion, disclaimer of opinion, qualified opinion by
 the auditor on the financial statements of, -

 i. the Listed Entity; or

 ii. any of the Listed Entity’s subsidiaries or associates, if the adverse
 opinion, disclaimer of opinion, qualified opinion has a material
 impact on the consolidated accounts of the Listed Entity.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 92, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.38
regulation_content.simple_explanation: If the auditor gives a negative, disclaimer or qualified opinion on the company's accounts, the company must disclose it immediately. The same applies to such an opinion on a subsidiary or associate if it materially affects the group accounts. These opinions are direct signals to investors about how trustworthy the numbers are.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Audit-opinion modifications are direct signals to investors about reliability of the numbers — the materiality filter on subsidiary/associate opinions keeps the obligation proportionate.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Disclose modified audit opinions immediately.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
93. Investigation

 (1) The Authority or a recognised stock exchange may require a Listed Entity
 to appoint a competent person to review or investigate its affairs and report
 its findings to the Authority, recognised stock exchange(s) and its Audit
 Committee.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall ensure that any information with respect to
 appointment of person as mentioned in sub regulation (1) and findings by
 such person, shall be immediately disclosed to the recognised stock
 exchange(s) for public dissemination.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 93, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.38
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The regulator or exchange can order a listed company to appoint a competent person to review or investigate its affairs and report back to the regulator, exchange and audit committee. The company must immediately disclose both the appointment and the findings publicly — it cannot keep either quiet.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is a supervisory-investigation power with a transparency tail — the entity cannot keep either the appointment or the findings private.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer / Audit Committee. Disclose the appointment and findings immediately.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
94. Encumbrances

 (1) The promoters and the controlling shareholders of the Listed Entity shall
 disclose details of any encumbrance of specified securities of the Listed
 Entity created or invoked or released, within two working days of such
 creation or invocation or release, as the case may be, to:

 (a) The recognised stock exchange (s); and

 (b) The Listed Entity.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall ensure that the disclosures received under sub-
 regulation (1) are immediately disclosed to the recognised stock
 exchange(s).
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 94, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.38
regulation_content.simple_explanation: If promoters or controlling shareholders pledge, un-pledge, or have their pledged shares taken over ('encumbrance' created, released or invoked), they must report it within 2 working days to the exchange and the company — and the company must then immediately pass it on to the exchange. This exposes hidden borrowing against big shareholders' stakes, which the market has a right to know about.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Encumbrance disclosure exposes hidden leverage on control blocks — a pledged promoter stake is a latent overhang the market is entitled to see. The obligation sits first on the promoter/controlling shareholder, with a relay duty on the entity.
regulation_content.practical_point: Set up a reporting channel for promoters and controlling shareholders keyed to the 2-working-day trigger, with the company relaying it on. Undisclosed promoter pledges are a classic blind spot inspectors probe.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Promoters and controlling shareholders (with entity relay). Trigger: encumbrance created/invoked/released. Deadline: within 2 working days.
regulation_content.risk_point: Undisclosed promoter pledges are a classic governance blind spot that inspections and investors probe.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Encumbrance disclosure within 2 working days of creation, invocation or release
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
95. Shareholding Pattern

 The Listed Entity shall submit its shareholding pattern to the recognised stock
 exchange(s), in such form and manner as may be specified by the Authority or
 the recognised stock exchange(s) on a quarterly basis, within fifteen working
 days from the end of each quarter.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 95, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.38
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Every quarter, the company must file its shareholding pattern (who owns how much) with the exchange, within 15 working days of the quarter-end. It is a routine, calendar-driven filing — the only real discipline is not missing the deadline.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: A recurring, calendar-driven filing — the fifteen-working-day window is generous, but the discipline is not missing the quarterly cadence.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Frequency: quarterly, within 15 working days of quarter-end.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Shareholding pattern within 15 working days of each quarter-end
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
96. Financial Statements

 (1) The Listed Entity shall disclose the audited standalone and consolidated
 financial statements for the full financial year to the recognised stock
 exchange(s) immediately after the approval of its board of directors, but in
 any event not later than three months of the end of financial year.

 (2) [The Listed Entity shall disclose the financial statements for first half of the
 financial year to the recognised stock exchange(s) immediately after the
 approval of its board of directors, but in any event not later than forty five
 days after the end of first half year.]5

 (3) The Listed Entity shall prepare its financial statements in accordance with
 IFRS or US GAAP or Ind AS or other accounting standards as applicable
 in its home jurisdiction:

 Provided that a Listed Entity preparing financial statements as per the
 accounting standards of its home jurisdiction (other than IFRS, US GAAP
 and Ind AS) shall be required to reconcile the same with IFRS.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 96, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.38
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must publish its financial results twice a year. The full-year audited results (both standalone and group) go out as soon as the board approves them, and no later than 3 months after year-end. The half-year results go out within 45 days of the first half ending. Big change: on 14 October 2025, the earlier requirement of quarterly results within 45 days was replaced by this half-yearly rule — so there are now only two reporting points a year, not four.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The 14-Oct-2025 amendment replaced quarterly-within-45-days with a half-yearly-within-45-days regime — a material easing of the periodic-reporting burden for IFSC Listed Entities. Update reporting calendars accordingly; the old three-quarter cadence no longer applies.
regulation_content.practical_point: Reset the results calendar to just two dates — annual within 3 months, half-yearly within 45 days — and retire the old quarterly-results assumption, so you neither over-report nor miss the half-year deadline.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer / Board. Frequency: annual within 3 months of FY-end; half-yearly within 45 days of first half.
regulation_content.example: For a company with a 31 March year-end: full-year results are due by 30 June, and half-year results (to 30 September) are due by about mid-November — with no separate first-quarter or third-quarter filing anymore.
regulation_content.risk_point: Running the pre-amendment quarterly calendar risks either over-reporting or, worse, missing the correct half-yearly deadline.
regulation_content.interview_point: How did the 14-Oct-2025 amendment change the periodic financial-reporting cadence under Reg 96, and what are the two remaining reporting points?
regulation_content.important_numbers: Annual audited financials within 3 months of FY-end; half-yearly financials within 45 days of first half-year (w.e.f. 14-Oct-2025; earlier quarterly within 45 days)
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 97, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.39
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must send its annual report to the exchange as soon as it is finalised and put it on its website. The report must include the audited standalone and group accounts, the directors' report, a management discussion, its corporate-governance practices, a sustainability report (where required) and anything its home country mandates. Because these contents are fixed, the governance and sustainability information cannot be hidden away.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The annual report is the composite governance document — its prescribed contents mean the corporate-governance and sustainability disclosures cannot be relegated to a website corner.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Frequency: annual. Submit to exchange and publish on website.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
98. Statement of deviation(s) or variation(s)

 (1) The Listed Entity shall submit to the recognised stock exchange(s) the
 statement(s) of deviation (indicating category wise variation between
 projected utilisation of funds made by it in its offer document), if any, in
 the use of proceeds from the objects stated in the offer document on a
 quarterly basis for public issue.

 (2) The statement(s) specified in sub-regulation (1), shall be continued to be
 given till such time the issue proceeds have been fully utilised or the
 purpose for which these proceeds were raised has been achieved.

 (3) The statement(s) specified in sub-regulation (1), shall be submitted to the
 recognised stock exchange(s) immediately after review by the audit
 committee but not later than forty five days from the end of quarter.

 (4) The Listed Entity shall furnish an explanation for the variation specified in

5 Substituted by the IFSCA (Listing) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, w.e.f. 14th October,

2025. Prior to its substitution, it read as under:
“(2) The Listed Entity shall disclose the financial statements for each of the first three quarters
of its financial year to the recognised stock exchange(s) immediately after the approval of its
board of directors, but in any event not later than forty five days after the end of each quarter.”

 sub-regulation (1), in the directors’ report in the annual report.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 98, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.39
regulation_content.simple_explanation: If a company raised money in a public issue, it must file a quarterly statement showing whether it actually spent the money on what it told investors it would — continuing until the money is fully used. This goes out within 45 days of each quarter-end, after the audit committee reviews it, with any difference explained in the directors' report. It closes the loop between the promise and the actual spending.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This closes the loop between what the issuer told investors it would do with the money and what it actually did — the audit-committee review is the internal control that gives the statement credibility.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer / Audit Committee. Frequency: quarterly, within 45 days, until full utilisation (public issues).
regulation_content.important_numbers: Deviation statement within 45 days of quarter-end
regulation_content.compliance_frequency: Quarterly (within 45 days of quarter-end, for public issues)
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
99. Corporate Governance

 (1) The Listed Entity shall describe its corporate governance practices in its
 annual report in the manner specified by the laws of the jurisdiction of its
 incorporation.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall also comply with the corporate governance norms
 as may be specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 99, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.40
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must describe its corporate-governance practices in its annual report, following its home-country law, and also follow any governance rules the regulator sets. So a foreign company cannot rely on its home rules alone if the regulator asks for more.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Governance disclosure is home-jurisdiction-anchored but overlaid by Authority norms — a foreign issuer cannot rely solely on its home framework if the Authority specifies more.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
100. Sustainability Report

 (1) The Listed Entity shall disclose to the recognised stock exchange(s) a
 sustainability report with respect to environmental, social and governance
 factors for financial year, no later than six months after the end of its
 financial year:

 Provided that this sub-regulation shall not apply to the Listed Entities
 having market capitalisation of less than USD 50 million.

 (2) The sustainability report specified in sub-regulation (1) shall be prepared
 based on:

 (a) internationally accepted reporting standards such as Global Reporting
 Initiative, International Sustainability Standards Board, Task Force on
 Climate-related Financial Disclosures;

 (b) Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting; or

 (c) any other standards that may be specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 100, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.40
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must publish a sustainability report on its ESG (environmental, social, governance) performance within 6 months of year-end, using an accepted standard (like GRI, ISSB, TCFD or BRSR). Small companies — those worth under USD 50 million — are exempt. That size threshold tells a smaller company whether it needs to build ESG-reporting systems at all.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The USD 50 million market-cap exemption is the practical filter — below it, sustainability reporting is optional, which matters for smaller foreign issuers deciding how much ESG infrastructure to build.
regulation_content.practical_point: Check the company's market value against the USD 50 million line to decide if this applies, then pick a reporting standard and set a reminder for 6 months after year-end.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Frequency: annual, within 6 months of FY-end (unless below USD 50 million market cap).
regulation_content.important_numbers: Sustainability report within 6 months of FY-end; exemption below USD 50 million market cap
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
101. Corporate actions

 (1) The Listed Entity shall inform the recognised stock exchange(s) in advance
 of any proposed corporate actions such as stock split, consolidation,
 dividend, bonus issues or similar events.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall give notice of the record date for such corporate
 action to the recognised stock exchange(s), wherever applicable at least
 three working days in advance, specifying the purpose of the record date.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 101, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.40
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Before a corporate action (like a stock split, bonus, or dividend), the company must tell the exchange in advance and give at least 3 working days' notice of the 'record date' — the cut-off date that decides which shareholders are entitled. The 3-day notice gives the market and intermediaries time to work out who qualifies.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The three-working-day record-date notice is a settlement-and-entitlement safeguard — it gives the market and intermediaries time to identify entitled holders.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Record-date notice ≥3 working days in advance.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Record-date notice ≥3 working days in advance
regulation_content.compliance_frequency: Event-based (record date notice ≥3 working days advance)
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
102. Meetings of shareholders and voting

 (1) The Listed Entity shall provide the remote e-voting facility to its
 shareholders in respect of all shareholders' resolutions.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall submit the voting results to the recognised stock
 exchange(s), within two working days from the date of conclusion of its
 General Meeting.

 (3) The Listed Entity shall send proxy forms to holders of the securities in all
 cases, mentioning that a holder may vote either for or against each
 resolution.

 (4) The Listed Entity shall provide one-way live webcast of the proceedings of
 the annual general meetings to all its shareholders.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 102, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.40
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must make it easy for shareholders to vote. It must offer remote electronic voting on every resolution, report the voting results to the exchange within 2 working days of the meeting, send proxy forms that let shareholders vote for or against each item, and provide a live webcast of the annual meeting. Together these help a scattered, cross-border shareholder base take part.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The package is a shareholder-democracy standard — e-voting, timely results, proxy fairness and webcast together lower the barriers to participation for a geographically dispersed IFSC shareholder base.
regulation_content.practical_point: Provide e-voting and a webcast for all resolutions and annual meetings, and diarise the 2-working-day deadline to file voting results after each meeting.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Voting results within 2 working days of the GM; e-voting and webcast for all resolutions/AGMs.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Voting results within 2 working days of General Meeting
regulation_content.compliance_frequency: Event-based (voting results within 2 working days of GM)
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
103. Whistle-blower mechanism

 The Listed Entity shall establish a whistle-blower mechanism for directors,
 employees and others to report genuine concerns while ensuring adequate
 safeguards against victimisation of persons who use such mechanism.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 103, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.41
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must set up a whistle-blower channel so directors, employees and others can report genuine concerns — with protection against being punished for speaking up. That protection is what makes the channel real; without it, people stay silent.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The anti-victimisation safeguard is what makes the mechanism real rather than nominal — a channel without protection does not surface concerns.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
104. Website

 The Listed Entity shall maintain a functional website that contains basic
 information about the entity including details about its business, board of
 directors, key managerial personnel, compliance officer, financial statements,
 e-mail address for grievance redressal and annual reports.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 104, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.41
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must keep a working website with its basic information — what it does, its board and key managers, the Compliance Officer, its financial statements, a grievance email, and its annual reports. The grievance email and Compliance Officer details make the site a real contact point, not just a brochure.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The website is the baseline public-information utility; the grievance email and compliance-officer details make it a live investor-contact point, not a brochure.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Maintain and keep current the prescribed website content.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
105. Dissemination by recognised stock exchange(s)

 The recognised stock exchange(s) shall ensure that the disclosures made by the
 Listed Entities are immediately disseminated on their websites.

 PART C: SECONDARY LISTING OF SPECIFIED SECURITIES
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 105, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.41
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The exchange (not the company) must make sure listed companies' disclosures are put on its website immediately. This closes the loop so that what companies file actually reaches the market.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is an obligation on the exchange, not the issuer — it closes the dissemination loop so filings actually reach the market.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with specified securities listed as a primary listing

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.provision_heading: Disclosure by entities with secondary listing of specified securities
regulation_content.regulation_text:
106. Disclosure by entities with secondary listing of specified securities

 The issuer with secondary listing of specified securities on a recognised stock
 exchange shall comply with the following requirements:

 a) It shall ensure that the specified securities are continued to be listed
 on its home exchange and abide by the listing and other rules of such
 exchange and home regulator;

 b) It shall release all disclosures in English to the recognised stock
 exchange(s) simultaneously with their release to its home exchange
 and home regulator where it has a primary listing; and

 c) It shall comply with such other requirements as may be specified by
 the Authority or recognised stock exchange(s).

PART D - LISTING OBLIGATIONS AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS
FOR COMPANIES HAVING DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS LISTED ON
RECOGNISED STOCK EXCHANGE (S)
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 106, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.41
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with a secondary listing here must keep its shares listed on its home exchange and follow home rules, and must send every disclosure to the IFSC exchange in English at the same time as it releases it at home — plus meet any extra regulator or exchange requirements. Simultaneous English disclosure is the fairness anchor: IFSC investors must not hear material news later than the home market.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Simultaneous, English-language disclosure is the equal-treatment anchor for secondary listings — IFSC investors must not learn material information after the home market.
regulation_content.practical_point: Set the workflow so every home-market release goes to the IFSC exchange in English at the same moment, not afterwards, and keep the home listing in good standing.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Simultaneous English disclosure to the IFSC exchange with home-market release.
regulation_content.applicability: Entities with secondary listing of specified securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
107. Financial Statements

 (1) The Listed Entity shall disclose the audited financial statements for the full
 financial year to the recognised stock exchange(s) immediately after the
 approval of its board of directors, but in any event not later than three
 months of the end of financial year.

 (2) [The Listed Entity shall disclose the financial statements for first half of the
 financial year to the recognised stock exchange(s) immediately after the
 approval of its board of directors, but in any event not later than forty five

 days after the end of first half year.]6

 (3) The Listed Entity shall prepare its financial statements in accordance with
 IFRS or US GAAP or Ind AS or other accounting standards as applicable
 in its home jurisdiction:

 Provided that a Listed Entity preparing financial statements as per the
 accounting standards of its home jurisdiction (other than IFRS, US GAAP
 and Ind AS) shall be required to reconcile the same with IFRS.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 107, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.41
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with listed depository receipts (DRs) must publish full-year audited results within 3 months of year-end and half-year results within 45 days of the first half. Like Reg 96, the 14 October 2025 change moved this from quarterly to half-yearly reporting, so read the two together.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The DR periodic-reporting cadence was moved to half-yearly-within-45-days by the 14-Oct-2025 amendment, mirroring Reg 96 — the two provisions must be read as amended together.
regulation_content.practical_point: Use the same two dates as ordinary companies — annual within 3 months, half-yearly within 45 days — for the DR financial calendar.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer / Board. Annual within 3 months; half-yearly within 45 days.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Annual audited financials within 3 months; half-yearly financials within 45 days (w.e.f. 14-Oct-2025; earlier quarterly within 45 days)
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
108. Material or price sensitive events

 (1) The Listed Entity shall immediately make disclosure to the recognised
 stock exchange(s) of any event or information concerning it or any of its
 subsidiaries or associates which, in the opinion of the board of directors of
 the Listed Entity, is material or price sensitive.

 Explanation 1: The Listed Entity shall consider the following criteria for
 determination of materiality of events/ information:

 (a) the omission of an event or information, which is likely to result
 in discontinuity or alteration of event or information already
 available publicly;

 (b) the omission of an event or information which is likely to result in
 significant market reaction if the said omission came to light at a
 later date; or

 (c) where the criteria specified in sub-clauses (a) and (b) are not
 applicable, an event/information may be treated as being material
 if in the opinion of the board of directors of Listed Entity, the event
 / information is considered material.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall frame a policy for determination of materiality
 based on criteria specified in these regulations, duly approved by its board
 of directors, which shall be disclosed on its website.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 108, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.42
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with listed DRs must immediately disclose anything important or price-sensitive, using the same materiality test and 24-hour discipline as ordinary listed companies (Reg 87), and keep a board-approved, published materiality policy.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The DR materiality regime tracks Reg 87 — the same twenty-four-hour discipline and materiality reasoning apply, adapted to the DR structure.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Immediate disclosure of material/price-sensitive events.
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
109. Shareholding pattern

 The Listed Entity shall submit its shareholding pattern to the recognised stock
 exchange(s), in the format specified by the Authority or by such recognised
 stock exchange(s) on a quarterly basis, within fifteen working days from the end
 of each quarter.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 109, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.42
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with listed DRs must file its shareholding pattern with the exchange every quarter, within 15 working days of the quarter-end — the DR version of Reg 95.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Quarterly, within 15 working days of quarter-end.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Shareholding pattern within 15 working days of each quarter-end
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
110. Corporate Governance

 (1) The Listed Entity shall describe its corporate governance practices in its
 annual report in the manner specified by the relevant laws in its home
 jurisdiction.

6 Substituted by the IFSCA (Listing) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, w.e.f. 14th October,

2025. Prior to its substitution, it read as under:
“(2) The Listed Entity shall disclose the financial statements for each of the first three quarters
of its financial year to the recognised stock exchange(s) immediately after the approval of its
board of directors, but in any event not later than forty five days after the end of each quarter.”

 (2) The Listed Entity shall also comply with the corporate governance norms
 as may be specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 110, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.42
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with listed DRs must describe its corporate-governance practices in its annual report under its home-country law, and follow any governance rules the regulator sets — the DR version of Reg 99.
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
111. Change of depository bank

 (1) The Listed Entity shall take prior approval of the recognised stock
 exchange(s) before changing its depository bank.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall disclose any change of depository bank to the
 recognised stock exchange(s) within twenty four hours of such change.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 111, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.43
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with listed DRs must get the exchange's approval before it changes its depository bank (the bank that holds the underlying shares and issues the receipts), and must disclose any such change within 24 hours. Because that bank sits between DR holders and the real shares, a change is both an approval matter and a fast-disclosure matter.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The depository bank sits between the DR holders and the underlying, so a change is both a prior-approval and a rapid-disclosure event.
regulation_content.practical_point: Get exchange approval before switching depository bank, and keep a 24-hour disclosure ready for when the change takes effect.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Prior approval for depository-bank change; disclose within 24 hours.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Change of depository bank disclosed within 24 hours (prior approval required)
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
112. Corporate actions

 (1) The Listed Entity shall inform the recognised stock exchange(s) in advance
 of any proposed corporate action pertaining to the depository receipts or the
 underlying securities.

 (2) The Listed Entity shall give notice of the record date to the recognised stock
 exchange(s), wherever applicable, at least three working days in advance,
 specifying the purpose of the record date.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 112, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.43
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with listed DRs must give the exchange advance notice of corporate actions on the DRs or the underlying shares, with at least 3 working days' notice of the record date — the DR version of Reg 101.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer. Record-date notice ≥3 working days in advance.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Record-date notice ≥3 working days in advance
regulation_content.compliance_frequency: Event-based (record date notice ≥3 working days advance)
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
113. Other compliances

 The Listed Entity shall comply with following additional requirements:

 a) Where the underlying specified securities are listed on its home
 exchange, it shall abide by the listing and other rules of such exchange
 and home regulator;

 b) It shall release all disclosures in English to the recognised stock
 exchange(s) simultaneously with their release to its home exchange
 or home regulator where it has a primary listing; and

 c) It shall comply with such other requirements as may be specified by
 the Authority or recognised stock exchange(s).
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 113, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.43
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A company with listed DRs must follow the home exchange's and home regulator's rules where the underlying shares are listed, send its English disclosures to the IFSC exchange at the same time as at home, and meet any further requirements. It mirrors Reg 106, with simultaneous English disclosure again the fairness anchor.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The DR analogue of Reg 106 — simultaneous English disclosure is again the equal-treatment anchor.
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
114. Voting Rights

 The voting rights of the depository receipts holders shall be exercised in
 accordance with the depository agreement.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 114, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.43
regulation_content.simple_explanation: DR holders vote according to the terms of the depository agreement — voting passes through the depository rather than being exercised directly. This is exactly the kind of DR-holder right that Reg 61 says must be spelled out clearly for investors up front.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Voting flows through the depository agreement, not directly to the DR holder — this is precisely the DR-holder-rights point that Reg 61 requires be disclosed up front.
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
115. Dissemination by recognised stock exchange(s)

 The recognised stock exchange(s) shall ensure that the disclosures made by the
 Listed Entities are immediately disseminated on their websites.

PART E - LISTING OBLIGATIONS AND CONTINUOUS DISCLOSURE
REQUIREMENTS FOR DEBT SECURITIES
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 115, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.43
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The exchange must make sure listed companies' disclosures are put on its website immediately — the DR-chapter version of Reg 105.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The DR analogue of Reg 105 — a dissemination duty on the exchange.
regulation_content.applicability: Companies with depository receipts listed on a recognised stock exchange

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
116. Material or price sensitive events

 (1) The issuer shall immediately disclose to the recognised stock exchange(s)
 all events which are material or price sensitive.

 (2) The issuer shall immediately disclose to the recognised stock exchange(s)

 the following events:

 (a) any redemption or cancellation of the debt securities;

 (b) details of any interest payment(s), except where the debt securities
 are having fixed rate;

 (c) any buy back or put option exercised;

 (d) any delay in payment of principal and/or interest amount; and

 (e) any modification in terms and conditions of the issue.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 116, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.43
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A debt (bond) issuer must immediately disclose anything important or price-sensitive — and specifically: any redemption or cancellation, interest payments (except fixed-rate), a buyback or put-option exercise, any delay in paying interest or principal, and any change to the terms of the issue. For bonds, the news that moves the price is about repayment, so a missed or delayed payment must never be hidden.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: For debt, the price-sensitive events are credit events — the delay-in-payment and terms-modification triggers are the ones that move a bond's price and must never be sat on.
regulation_content.practical_point: Build a bond-event checklist around payment status and any change in terms, and treat any payment delay as an immediate-disclosure event — a silent payment delay is the single worst debt-disclosure failure.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Compliance Officer / Issuer. Immediate disclosure of listed credit events.
regulation_content.risk_point: A silent payment delay is the cardinal debt-disclosure failure.
