regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of listed debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
117. Financial Statements

 (1) The issuer shall disclose the audited financial statements for the full
 financial year to the recognised stock exchange(s) immediately after the
 approval of its board of directors, but in any event not later than three
 months of the end of financial year.

 (2) The issuer shall prepare its financial statements in accordance with IFRS or
 US GAAP or Ind AS or other accounting standards as applicable in its home
 jurisdiction:

 Provided that an issuer preparing financial statements as per the accounting
 standards of its home jurisdiction (other than IFRS, US GAAP and Ind AS)
 shall be required to reconcile the same with IFRS.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 117, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.44
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A bond issuer must publish its audited full-year results within 3 months of year-end. For bonds, reporting is once a year only — there is no half-yearly requirement like for shares — reflecting what bond investors mainly need to know.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Debt periodic reporting is annual — there is no half-yearly financial obligation of the Reg 96 kind, reflecting the different information needs of debt investors.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Issuer / Board. Annual audited financials within 3 months of FY-end.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Debt: annual audited financials within 3 months of FY-end
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of listed debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
118. Annual Report

 The issuer shall submit to the recognised stock exchange(s) a copy of the annual
 report immediately after the finalisation of the same, but in any event not later
 than six months of the end of financial year.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 118, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.44
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A bond issuer must send its annual report to the exchange as soon as it is finalised, and no later than 6 months after year-end.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Issuer. Annual report within 6 months of FY-end.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Debt: annual report within 6 months of FY-end
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of listed debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
119. Revision in Credit Rating

 The issuer shall immediately disclose to the recognised stock exchange(s) any
 revision in the credit rating of its debt securities listed on such exchange(s).
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 119, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.44
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A bond issuer must immediately disclose any change in the credit rating of its listed bonds. A rating change is a direct signal to bond investors, so speed is the whole point — and it links back to the rating rules in Reg 72.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: A rating change is a direct price signal for debt — immediacy is the whole point, and it ties back to the rating architecture in Reg 72.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Issuer. Immediate disclosure of rating revisions.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of listed debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
120. Record Date

 The issuer shall disclose the record date relevant to the holders of debt securities
 in a timely manner.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 120, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.44
regulation_content.simple_explanation: A bond issuer must disclose, in good time, the record date that decides which bondholders are entitled to a payment, so entitlements can be worked out cleanly.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Issuer. Timely record-date disclosure.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of listed debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
121. Exempt Issuers

 A recognised stock exchange may, if satisfied on the basis of an application
 made by an issuer, relax the applicability of certain requirements of this chapter,
 in accordance with its internal policy or guidelines, for the following issuers:

 (a) Supranational, multilateral or statutory institutions
 /organizations /agencies; and

 (b) Entities whose securities are irrevocably guaranteed by a
 Sovereign; and

 (c) Any other entity as may be specified by the Authority from time
 to time.

 CHAPTER XIII: PERMITTED TO TRADE
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 121, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.44
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The exchange can, under a written policy, relax some Chapter XII duties for very high-quality public issuers (like multilateral institutions or government-guaranteed issuers, and others the regulator names) — the ongoing-disclosure version of the Reg 74 relaxation.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The continuous-disclosure analogue of the Reg 74 relaxation — high-credit public issuers get calibrated relief, controlled by the exchange's internal policy.
regulation_content.applicability: Issuers of listed debt securities

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
122. Permitted to Trade

 A recognised stock exchange may with prior approval of the Authority permit
 trading of securities without the involvement of the issuer, subject to the
 following conditions:

 (a) Such trading of securities is in conformity with the applicable
 laws of the jurisdictions in which the securities are listed; and

 (b) The recognised stock exchange(s) shall ensure clearing and
 settlement of the trades.

 CHAPTER XIV: MISCELLANEOUS
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 122, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.45
regulation_content.simple_explanation: With the regulator's prior approval, an exchange can allow certain securities to be traded here without the issuer being involved — as long as the trading follows the rules of the places where the securities are listed and the exchange handles clearing and settlement. It is a way to give investors access to securities the issuer has not itself brought to IFSC.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: 'Permitted to trade' is an exchange-driven access mechanism for securities the issuer has not itself brought to the IFSC market — the prior-approval and settlement conditions are what keep it orderly.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
123. Listing agreement

 The entity desirous of listing its securities and permitted financial products on
 the recognised stock exchange(s) shall execute a listing agreement with such
 stock exchange, in such form and manner as specified by such stock exchange.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 123, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.45
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Any company listing securities or products must sign a listing agreement with the exchange in the exchange's format. This agreement is the contract that binds the company to the exchange's rulebook alongside these regulations.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The listing agreement is the contractual overlay that binds the issuer to the exchange's rulebook alongside these regulations.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Owner: Issuer. Execute the listing agreement before listing.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
124. Refusal of admission to list

 A recognised stock exchange may, at its discretion, reject an application for
 admission to list securities or permitted financial products, if it considers that-

 (a) listing of such securities or permitted financial products would be
 detrimental to investors' interests; or

 (b) the issuer does not comply or will not comply with any requirement
 specified by the Authority or the recognised stock exchange.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 124, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.45
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An exchange can refuse a listing application if it thinks listing would harm investors, or that the company does not — or will not — follow the regulator's or exchange's requirements. The 'will not' part lets the exchange act on a likely future compliance problem, not just a current one.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: A gatekeeping discretion vested in the exchange — the 'will not comply' limb lets the exchange act on prospective, not just present, non-compliance.
regulation_content.risk_point: An issuer with a poor compliance trajectory faces refusal risk even before a specific breach.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
125. Suspension

 (1) A recognised stock exchange may suspend the trading of securities or
 permitted financial products where it appears that:

 (a) the issuer is in non-compliance with the regulatory provisions specified
 by the Authority or the recognised stock exchange;

 (b) the issuer has been suspended for trading of its securities by any other
 exchange; or

 (c) the suspension is required for ensuring orderly operation of its market.

 (2) A recognised stock exchange may restore trading of securities that have
 been suspended if it considers that the suspension is no longer required.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 125, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.45
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An exchange can suspend trading in a security if the company is non-compliant, if it has been suspended by another exchange, or if suspension is needed to keep the market orderly — and can restart trading once the reason is gone. Suspension is a protective tool, not a punishment, though a suspension by another exchange can trigger one here too.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Suspension is a market-integrity tool with a built-in restoration path — it is protective, not punitive, though the cross-exchange-suspension trigger imports another market's judgment.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
126. Voluntary Delisting

 A recognised stock exchange may delist securities, on receipt of the request
 from the Listed Entity, in such manner and subject to such conditions as may be
 specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 126, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.45
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An exchange can delist a company's securities at the company's own request ('voluntary delisting'), on the terms the regulator specifies. Those terms are left to the regulator and require public consultation (Reg 130), so this is a doorway pending detailed rules.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Voluntary delisting mechanics are left to Authority specification (and, per Reg 130(2), require public consultation) — treat this as a gateway pending detailed norms.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
127. Compulsory Delisting

 A recognised stock exchange may compulsorily delist securities or permitted
 financial products of the issuer under the following conditions:

 (a) The securities or permitted financial products have remained
 suspended for a period of more than six months;

 (b) the securities or permitted financial products have been compulsorily
 delisted by another exchange;

 (c) where the exchange is satisfied that there are special circumstances that
 require delisting of the securities or permitted financial products; or

 (d) it is directed to do so by the Authority or any other relevant authority
 or any court having jurisdiction in the matter.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 127, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.46
regulation_content.simple_explanation: An exchange can force a delisting ('compulsory delisting') if the securities have been suspended for more than 6 months, if another exchange has compulsorily delisted them, if special circumstances demand it, or if the regulator, another authority or a court so directs. The 6-month suspension is the clear-cut trigger; this is the final step in the ladder that runs from suspension to delisting.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The six-month suspension trigger is the objective limb; the others are discretion- or direction-led. Compulsory delisting is the terminal consequence in the enforcement ladder that runs suspension to delisting.
regulation_content.risk_point: A prolonged suspension approaching six months is the point at which continuation risk becomes acute.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Compulsory delisting where suspended > 6 months, among other grounds
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
128. Submission of information

 The issuer shall submit all information sought by the Authority or the recognised
 stock exchange(s) relating to securities market.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 128, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.46
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The company must provide whatever information the regulator or exchange asks for about the securities market. This broad duty backs up all the specific disclosure rules by ensuring the regulator and exchange can always ask for more.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: A broad information-production duty — it backstops the specific disclosure obligations by ensuring the regulator and exchange can always call for more.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.provision_heading: Power to exempt/ relax strict enforcement of the regulations
regulation_content.regulation_text:
129. Power to exempt/ relax strict enforcement of the regulations

 (1) The Authority may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, in the interest of
 investors or for the development of the financial market in IFSC, exempt/
 relax the strict enforcement of any requirement of these regulations.

 (2) For seeking exemption/ relaxation under sub-regulation (1), an application,
 giving details and the grounds on which such exemption/ relaxation has
 been sought, shall be filed with the Authority.

 (3) The application referred to under sub-regulation (2) shall be accompanied
 by such non-refundable fee as may be specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 129, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.46
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The regulator can, for written reasons and in the interest of investors or the IFSC market, exempt a company from a rule or relax how strictly it is enforced — but only on a formal application that gives the reasons and pays a set, non-refundable fee. This is a safety valve for genuine hard cases, not a routine shortcut.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is the general dispensing power — reasoned, application-based and fee-bearing. It is the pressure valve for genuine hard cases, not a routine workaround.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.provision_heading: Power to specify norms, procedures, issue clarifications and remove difficulties
regulation_content.regulation_text:
130. Power to specify norms, procedures, issue clarifications and remove
 difficulties

 (1) For the purposes of implementation of these regulations and matters
 incidental thereto, the Authority may specify norms, procedures, processes,
 additional requirements, etc. by way of circulars or guidelines or directions.

 (2) The requirements under regulations 80, 81, 82 and 126 may be specified
 after public consultation and approval in a meeting of the Authority.

 (3) In order to remove any difficulties in the application or interpretation of
 these regulations, the Authority may issue clarifications through guidance
 notes or circulars.
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 130, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.46
regulation_content.simple_explanation: The regulator can issue detailed rules, procedures and clarifications through circulars and guidance to make the framework work in practice. For four provisions — commercial paper (80), certificates of deposit (81), other products (82) and voluntary delisting (126) — the detailed rules must first go through public consultation and regulator approval. A lot of the real operating detail behind the enabling provisions lives in these circulars.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is the engine room of the regime — much of the operative detail for the enabling provisions lives in circulars issued under this power. The public-consultation gate for Regs 80, 81, 82 and 126 is a procedural safeguard worth citing.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)

regulation_content.regulation_name: International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024
regulation_content.regulation_text:
131. Repeal and Savings

 (1) On and from the commencement of these regulations, the International
 Financial Services Centres Authority (Issuance and Listing of Securities)

 Regulations, 2021 shall stand superseded.

(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulation (1), anything done
 or any action taken or purported to have been taken under the regulations
 mentioned in sub-regulation (1), before the commencement of these
 regulations shall be deemed to have been done or taken or commenced
 under the corresponding provisions of these regulations.

 K. Rajaraman, Chairperson
regulation_content.source_reference: Reg 131, International Financial Services Centres Authority (Listing) Regulations, 2024 (IFSCA/GN/2024/006, as amended up to 14-Oct-2025); source PDF p.46
regulation_content.simple_explanation: When these 2024 rules started, they replaced the older 2021 listing regulations. Anything validly done under the 2021 rules before that date is treated as done under the matching 2024 provision — so past filings and approvals stay valid and are not reopened. This is the provision to cite when lining up pre-2024 deals against the current rules.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The savings clause preserves continuity — actions validly taken under the 2021 framework carry over, so historic filings and approvals are not reopened by the supersession. This is the provision to cite when reconciling pre-2024 offer documents against the current regime.
regulation_content.practical_point: When reviewing older (pre-2024) transactions, match what was done under the 2021 rules to the equivalent 2024 provision rather than treating it as invalid.
regulation_content.applicability: All Listed Entities / issuers and the recognised stock exchange(s)
